intended_object: The absolute value on a field K induced by a ring embedding φ : K → A into a normed division ring, x ↦ ‖φ(x)‖ (the "place" associated to an embedding, e.g. an archimedean place of a number field from a complex embedding). Inferred from the docstring and usage in the InfinitePlace files.
explanation: The body pulls back the norm absolute value of A (`IsAbsoluteValue.toAbsoluteValue norm`) along the injective ring hom φ using `AbsoluteValue.comp`, giving exactly x ↦ ‖φ x‖. Injectivity is automatic because K is a field. The setting (any field K, any normed division ring A) is the natural generality: a multiplicative norm on A is needed, and injectivity is needed for positivity. Nothing restricts it to number fields beyond the namespace. It is correct in degenerate cases, since every absolute-value axiom is inherited from the norm.
